notes: Breadboard is drawn with rows 1-30 running down the page, so each image row N is catalogue column N; holes a-e are bank 't', f-j are bank 'b'. The left rails are named tp (red +) and tn (black -); rail index is counted from the top in groups of 5 (image 1: ground wire at tn.2, button ground at tn.1, supply red wire at tp.6, emitter wire at tn.10, battery at tp.25/tn.25).
Pi header pins are given as ports GPIO2, GPIO3, GPIO14 and GND (physical pin 6, the GND next to GP14 in the image). The 'GPIO_HEADER' port in the catalogue is not used.
The pushbutton straddles the centre gap: side 1 (1.l/1.r) in row 1 (1t.e and 1b.f), side 2 in row 3. Ground is on row 1 (1t.a) and GPIO14 on row 3 (3t.a).

Transistor 1 sits in column e rows 10/11/12 = emitter/collector/base. The 330Ω resistor runs 12c to 16c and GPIO2 is wired to 16a. The images show no explicit part at rows 6 and 11 for the balloon heater; the speaker cable cores from the balloon's 12Ω resistor are assumed to plug into row 6 (supply, via red jumper to + rail) and row 11 (collector strip).

The second balloon has no image. Its layout (transistor 2 at rows 20-22, 330Ω 22c-26c, GPIO3 at 26a, emitter jumper at 20a, supply jumper at 18a, cable ends at 18b and 21b) is my assumption by repeating the first balloon's wiring.
The parts list gives 8 pin-to-pin and 6 pin-to-socket jumpers, but only the 5 and 4 that the wiring requires are modelled.

Only one roll of electrical tape exists in the parts list; it is used for both balloons. Cable ends are twisted to the 12Ω resistor legs (either core to either leg). The 12Ω resistor is off-board on the balloon.
